extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent agents/attorneys, applicants, patent examiners, and patent bar candidates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing and prosecuting reissue applications and certificates of correction to correct errors in granted U.S. patents, including claim broadening, inventorship corrections, required content, examinations, and statutory/regulatory effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application may be filed to correct an error made without any deceptive intent in the original patent. In order to qualify for reissue, the patent must be deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid as a result of the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common reasons for filing a reissue include too narrow or too broad claims, inaccuracies in the disclosure, an incorrectly claimed foreign priority, or failure to make reference to or incorrectly making reference to prior copending applications. Reissues may not be filed for minor typing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue Claims Must Be for Same General Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue claims must be for the same general invention as claimed in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP section 1412.01 — reissue cannot claim a different general invention than the surrendered original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening Reissue Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadening claims refer to amending a patent’s claims during reissue to expand their scope to cover more subject matter than originally claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadening reissue claims are governed by specific rules (see MPEP 1412.03). Broadening is allowed only under statutory/regulatory constraints and may implicate intervening rights and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture of Canceled Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Recapture concerns attempting to reclaim subject matter that was canceled from original claims during reissue prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1412.02 for rules and limitations on recapturing canceled subject matter in a reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Inventorship by Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue may be used to correct inventorship on a patent by adding, removing, or otherwise amending the named inventors when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1412.04 and 1412.05 cover correction of inventorship generally and in the context of broadening reissues; formal requirements and statements/declarations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Reissue Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application must include a reissue specification, drawings (if necessary), and any amendments necessary to correct the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.173 and MPEP 1410 and following (1410.01–1410.03). The application must include required oaths/declarations, revised specification and any claim amendments and must comply with form and content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue Oath or Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application must include an inventor's (or applicant's) oath or declaration; content requirements may vary depending on filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1414.01–1414.03 for specifics on required statements, differences for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, and supplemental oaths/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of Specification and New Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue specification must be in proper form and must not introduce new matter beyond the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1411 and 1411.01–1411.02; adding 'new matter' is prohibited — reissue can correct but not add wholly new disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee Consent to the Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignee consent to the reissue may be required or relevant when rights have been assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1411.01 regarding circumstances where assignee consent is addressed; the MPEP identifies how assignee actions affect reissue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of Correction for Minor Errors
rubrics_metrics.description: A Certificate of Correction is an official document issued by the patent office to correct minor errors in a granted patent, such as typographical mistakes or inaccuracies in the inventor’s name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1480–1486 distinguish Office-attributable errors (1480, with expedited issuance 1480.01) from applicant mistakes (1481, 1481.01–1481.03). Handling procedures, corrections to assignee names, named inventors, and priority benefit corrections are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.121 — Manner of making amendments in application
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.121 details the specific procedures and formats required for making amendments to a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulation prescribes how to present amendments to claims, specifications, and drawings so they are acceptable to the Office; reissue filings/amendments must conform to these procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.173 — Reissue specification, drawings, and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.173 outlines the requirements for submitting a reissue application, including providing a revised specification, drawings, and any necessary amendments to correct errors in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with 1.173 is required for form and content of reissue submissions; see MPEP references to 1.173 for application-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 252 — Effect of reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissued patent replaces the original and retains its effect for the unexpired term, while protecting intervening rights for those who began using the invention before the reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP sections (e.g., 1456,1460) discuss the statutory effect and implications for third parties and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 253 — Disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 253 allows a patent holder to formally disclaim or dedicate to the public any complete claim or terminal part of the term of a patent, effectively narrowing the scope or duration of the patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers and their interaction with reissue/correction processes are addressed in MPEP 1490 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence in Filing Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligence in filing a reissue application is a considered factor — there are MPEP provisions on the appropriate timeliness and circumstances for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1403 (Diligence in Filing) for expectations and examples of when reissue should be sought and timeliness considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Physical Surrender of Original Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedurally, the original patent is surrendered for reissue purposes but there is no requirement of physically surrendering the original patent document in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1416 for the practice and implications regarding surrender of the original patent during reissue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue and Patent Term
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue can affect patent term considerations and interactions with maintenance fees and unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1405 and 1415 discuss how reissue affects patent term, issue fees, and maintenance fee implications; 35 U.S.C. 252 also relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and Consideration of References Cited in Original Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: References cited in the original patent must be cited and considered during reissue examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1406 for examiner obligations and how prior art cited in the original is treated in reissue examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of Reissue Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application is examined in essentially the same manner as an original application, including initial examiner review and consideration of prior art and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1440–1446 cover examination procedures, initial examiner review (1443), review of reissue oath/declaration (1444), and that reissue applications are examined similarly to original applications (1445).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Month Delay Period; Protest and Pre-issuance Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue filings may be subject to a two-month delay period and procedures for protests and third-party pre-issuance submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1441 and 1441.01 for the two-month delay and handling of protests/pre-issuance submissions in reissue contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Status — Litigation-Related or PTAB Trial-Related Reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue applications may receive special status when related to litigation or PTAB trials, with distinct procedural treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1442 and subparts (1442.01–1442.05) discuss special status, concurrent proceedings, stays, and court-ordered filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud, Inequitable Conduct, or Duty of Disclosure Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue prosecution may raise issues of alleged fraud, inequitable conduct, or duty of disclosure that must be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1448 for how such allegations impact reissue processing and examiner duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Prior/Concurrent Proceedings and Material Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must notify the Office of prior or concurrent proceedings and of information known to be material to patentability when filing reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1418 outlines notification obligations for concurrent proceedings and material information; failure to notify may have consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction and Election of Species in Reissue Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements and election of species may apply to reissue applications when multiple species are claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1450 for how restriction and election practice applies to reissue proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional and Continuation Reissue Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules govern divisional reissue applications and continuation reissue filings where the parent is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1451 covers divisional reissue applications and continuation practices and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) and Amendments in Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures exist for requesting continued examination and for making amendments to reissue applications during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1452 (RCE), 1453–1454 (amendments), and 1452–1454 for timing and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal, Allowance, Issue, and Reissue Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue applications have defined appeal routes, allowance and issue procedures, and provisions for reissue review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1454–1457 and 1455 discuss appeal briefs, allowance/issue processing, and post-allowance reissue review mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Reissue Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are specific provisions for design patent reissue applications and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1457 and 1458 for rules specific to design reissues and reserved sections that may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Reissue and Public Access/Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of reissue on public rights and the public availability of reissue files and Official Gazette notices are governed by MPEP provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 1460 on effect of reissue and 1430–1430.01 regarding reissue files open to the public and notices announced in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Requests for Certificates of Correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures govern how requests for certificates of correction are handled, whether office-attributable or applicant-attributable errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1485–1486 and related sections outline handling, processing, and distinctions between types of corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal disclaimers are a mechanism referenced in the context of reissue and correction practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 1490 and related provisions discuss disclaimers, their form, and interaction with reissue/correction remedies.
